title: MulBERRY: Enabling Bit-Error Robustness for Energy-Efficient Multi-Agent Autonomous Systems
problem: Autonomous UAV swarms operate under tight power constraints where voltage reduction improves energy efficiency but causes on-chip bit failures that degrade mission safety and performance. These swarms must execute complex reinforcement learning models while maintaining strict size, weight, and power constraints.
motivation: Autonomous swarms increasingly deployed in military and civilian applications require energy-efficient operation without sacrificing mission-critical robustness.
method: Reducing a chip's voltage saves power but causes random bit errors—flipped 0s and 1s in calculations. MulBERRY adds protections that catch and fix these bit errors in the reinforcement learning AI (where AI learns by trial and error) that coordinates multi-agent drone swarms. This lets the swarms keep operating safely even with power turned down to the minimum.
key_novelty: The key idea is making multi-agent reinforcement learning robust to bit errors—random corrupted calculations caused by low electrical power.
contributions: Bit-error robustness framework for RL models in multi-agent autonomous systems
Techniques for maintaining mission safety and performance under reduced-voltage operation
Evaluation methodology for energy-efficient autonomous swarms with hardware-level fault tolerance
primary_theme: Robust energy-efficient inference for autonomous swarms
